brief_summary: 2x2 matrix sub-grid mechanism diagram. Three switch junctions (row0/col0, row0/col1, row1/col0) are marked as real presses in coral with dashed current-path arrows tracing the backfeed route; the fourth junction (row1/col1) is drawn as a dashed warm-red outline circle labeled 'the ghost' to show the phantom key the controller reads despite no physical press there.
data_sources: key-matrix-ghosting-deep-dive.mdx § 'The three-key rectangle that creates a ghost' — 'Press the switches at row 0/column 0, row 0/column 1, and row 1/column 0 ... The controller, scanning column 1 and reading row 1, now sees a closed connection where no switch was pressed — the fourth corner.'
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Key_rollover — 'Key ghosting occurs on matrix keyboards for certain combinations of three keys' when 'three corners of a rectangular set of switches are closed.'
https://develop-docs.qmk.fm/how_a_matrix_works — matrix walkthrough reaching the identical three-key, four-position reading with no diodes present.
